methodological_rigor.justification: The GEMINI study uses a prospective service evaluation of 10,889 women with live AI integration plus simulation of 17 a-priori-specified workflows, pre-specified primary workflow, pre-specified Statistical Analysis Plan, and an independent Trusted Research Environment (DaSH) separating the evaluation team from the AI vendor. Statistical methods are appropriate: Wilson 95% CIs, bootstrap (50,000 reps) two-sided 90% CIs, pre-specified non-inferiority (margin 0.1) and gated superiority testing, an a priori sample size calculation (65 confirmed positives for 91.5% power), and a sensitivity analysis assuming fewer additional cancers. Limitations are explicitly acknowledged: single UK region/single AI tool, triage workflows only simulated (no behavioral response captured), 4,992 (29.1%) women excluded due to an IT timeout error (with a bias check showing no significant CDR/recall difference), 10.4% mammograms outside AI inclusion criteria, and thresholds not recalibrated before the study due to governance constraints. These gaps (single-site, simulation-based triage, vendor-supplied threshold) prevent a 5 but the design is solid and transparent.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual prospective cohort / service evaluation of a commercial AI system within a real routine NHS breast screening program, not a randomized trial, which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: the primary workflow increased CDR by 1 per 1,000 (10.4% relative), maintained recall rate, and cut workload up to 31%, with three other combined workflows showing superiority across all five metrics and workload savings of 33-36%. Findings directly inform how UK breast screening services could integrate AI and are consistent with MASAI and Danish real-world data cited in the discussion. It is not practice-changing on its own (single site, single vendor, no interval-cancer follow-up yet) so a 4 rather than 5 is appropriate.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript explicitly states adherence to the STARD-AI reporting statement and references a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary, with a detailed CONSORT-style flow (Fig. 1), pre-specified workflows, OPs, gating strategy (Table 5), sample-size calculation, and clearly reported CDR/recall/sensitivity/specificity/PPV with 95% CIs across all 17 workflows. Key STARD items are addressed (reference standard: histologically confirmed cancers; inclusion flow; exclusions with reasons; index test description of Mia v.3; thresholds). Data availability is strong: R code is deposited on Zenodo (ref 22, CFdeVries/gemini-paper), source data for Fig. 3 is released, and de-identified data reside in the DaSH Trusted Research Environment (which appropriately constrains raw patient data sharing). Minor gaps (no full STARD-AI checklist shown; interval cancer follow-up pending) keep this at 4.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript positions itself after MASAI, ScreenTrustCAD, and the Danish real-world data (refs 2, 3, 8) and its incremental novelty lies in simultaneously modeling 17 AI deployment configurations - including combined triage-negatives plus additional-read workflows - within one prospective UK cohort, rather than testing a single implementation strategy. The combination of live AI-Additional Read with simulated triage workflows to allow site-specific trade-offs between CDR, recall and workload is a meaningful methodological extension rather than a first-in-class finding. The core result (AI adds ~1 per 1,000 cancers and saves ~31-44% workload) recapitulates known effects from the cited trials, so novelty is real but bounded; a 4 rather than 5 is appropriate and guards against leniency.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, logically organized (Methods / Results by workflow family / Discussion with explicit limitations), and uses well-structured tables (cohort characteristics, arbitration time bands, 6+11 workflow performance tables, gating table) plus three figures (flow diagram, study design, workload bars). Terminology (OP1-4, AI-Additional Read, triage vs triage negatives, primary workflow) is defined on first use and used consistently. Tables 3 and 4 are information-dense and rely on cell shading that is only described in legends, which is a minor readability cost, and some methods prose (gating strategy paragraph) is dense. Overall it is publication-ready with minor tightening needed, meriting a 4.

key_strengths: Prospective real-world evaluation of 10,889 NHS screening attendees with live AI integration detecting 11 additional cancers beyond routine double reading
Pre-specified primary workflow, Statistical Analysis Plan, sample-size calculation (65 confirmed positives, 91.5% power) and gated non-inferiority/superiority testing with bootstrap CIs
Systematic assessment of 17 a-priori-specified AI workflows (2 additional-read, 5 triage, 10 combinations) enabling site-specific trade-offs between CDR, recall and workload
Independence from AI vendor enforced via a Trusted Research Environment (DaSH) with a separate vendor workspace, plus Zenodo-deposited R code and Fig. 3 source data
Explicit adherence to STARD-AI reporting and a transparent flow diagram with a bias check for the 4,992 cases lost to an IT timeout (no significant CDR or recall difference)
key_concerns: Single UK region and a single commercial AI system (Mia v.3), limiting external generalizability as acknowledged by the authors
Triage and triage-negatives workflows are simulated on retrospective AI output, so human behavioral responses to AI-as-second-reader are not captured
29.1% of women (4,992) lost to AI assessment due to an IT session-timeout coding error, and an additional 10.4% excluded by AI's own inclusion criteria

AI operating thresholds were not recalibrated for the current mammography software version prior to the study due to governance constraints, and interval-cancer follow-up is not yet available to confirm true sensitivity
No multiplicity correction across the 17 workflows (justified by a priori gating), so secondary-workflow superiority claims should be read with mild caution
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorously pre-specified prospective NHS evaluation that credibly demonstrates AI-enabled CDR gains and workload savings across 17 configurations, with strong reporting, independent analysis, and code release; single-site/single-vendor scope and simulated triage temper practice-changing status but the scale, design and clinical signal are consistent with top-tier oncology/medicine venues, and the remaining issues are addressable with minor revisions.
